questions.q: Per this lesson, what recurring design question did the Meridian Fixtures (ERP) case study mainly turn on?
options: Data volatility -- how often a specific field actually changes, and whether that justifies a live callout or a batch sync
Bidirectional coordination between two systems that can both originate changes
Trust boundaries between an external caller and Salesforce
Delivery guarantees under at-least-once event delivery
questions.explain: Meridian's case study was built around deciding, field by field, whether a real-time callout or a batch sync fit that field's actual rate of change -- a data-volatility question, not a delivery-guarantee or trust-boundary one.

questions.q: Which recurring design question does this lesson say the Vantage Utilities (external application) case study mainly turned on?
options: Consistency requirements for an analytics consumer
Data volatility of catalog and price fields
Trust boundaries -- who's calling, what they're allowed to do, and how that's enforced rather than assumed
Idempotent handling of duplicate financial events
questions.explain: Because Vantage's integration involved an external caller acting on behalf of individual customers, its defining question was about trust boundaries: verifying identity and enforcing per-customer authorization rather than assuming it.

questions.q: How does this lesson describe the relationship between Chapter 1's five case studies and the rest of the course?
options: They are five unrelated case studies with no connection to Chapters 2 and 3's material
They are one workflow (scope, design, review, document, present, defend) demonstrated five times on different problems so the underlying pattern becomes visible
They exist only to teach Salesforce-specific trivia with no general applicability
Each case study introduces a completely separate, non-overlapping workflow
questions.explain: The lesson explicitly frames the course as one workflow taught across thirteen lessons, with the five case studies as different vehicles for teaching the same underlying recurring questions and the same review-and-presentation process.

questions.q: What does this lesson say transfers to an integration case this course never specifically covered?
options: Nothing -- the lessons only apply to the exact five fictional companies covered
Only the specific company names and industries used in the case studies
Only the choice of Platform Events as an integration mechanism

The underlying workflow itself: naming system of record per field, matching pattern to volatility/consistency needs, naming failure categories, asking the four security questions, documenting the decision, and answering honestly under questioning
questions.explain: The lesson states explicitly that the specific systems (ERP, ledger, warehouse, portal, marketing platform) won't cover every future integration, but the workflow itself -- scoping, pattern selection, failure and security review, documentation, and honest defense -- does transfer.

questions.q: How does this lesson describe Lesson 14's mock review board relative to Chapter 1's five case studies?
options: It presents a new scenario that doesn't map one-to-one onto any single Chapter 1 case study, requiring the whole workflow to be run fresh under real-time questioning
It repeats one of the five case studies exactly, with no new elements
It removes the need for any security review
It is a written-only exercise with no live questioning involved
questions.explain: The lesson frames Lesson 14 as a fresh scenario, not a repeat of a memorized case study -- the goal is applying the full workflow under the same kind of live questioning Lesson 12 covered, not recognizing a pattern that's already been solved.
